## Motivation

Some kernels are specialized for one model, configuration and platform, and replace a model's whole step. They come from external libraries that load as SGLang plugins:

- the NVIDIA megakernel, from [sgl-nvidia-mega](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega)
- the AMD monokernels, from [sgl-amd-mono](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono)

Today these plugins serve small-batch decode and verify steps. Nothing ties them to low latency or to "mega" fusion; prefill or high-throughput specializations would plug in the same way.

SGLang's side of each integration lived in `srt/megakernels` and `srt/monokernels`. This PR splits that code at the kernel/runtime boundary:

- what a plugin implements and registers moves to `kernels/plugin_kernels/<hardware>/`, recorded by a new `KernelBackend.PLUGIN` (as with `kda_kernels/` and `cake_kernels/`)
- SGLang's serving integration stays in `srt/`, as `srt/kernel_plugins/<hardware>/`

The kernels themselves stay in their libraries.

## Modifications

```
python/sglang/kernels/plugin_kernels/   # the contract a plugin implements; imports nothing from srt
  nvidia/spec.py                        #   registration, API version, requirements, capabilities,
  amd/spec.py                           #   widths, build/forward contract
                                        #   (<hardware>/<model>/ for thin kernel wrappers later)
python/sglang/srt/kernel_plugins/       # SGLang's integration, one binding.py per hardware
  nvidia/binding.py                     #   startup checks on the resolved config, build, TP agreement,
  amd/binding.py                        #   CUDA graph coverage, forward dispatch with fallback,
                                        #   weight observation (AMD), the runtime state handed to a plugin
```

- **Move.** The code moves unchanged; only imports are combined.
  - `srt/{megakernels,monokernels}/spec.py` → `kernels/plugin_kernels/{nvidia,amd}/spec.py`.
  - Each hardware's `guards.py` + `runtime.py` (and, on NVIDIA, `binding.py`) → `srt/kernel_plugins/<hardware>/binding.py`.
  - Unit tests → `test/registered/unit/kernel_plugins/{nvidia,amd}/`. They now patch the one `binding` module.
- **No aliases.** `sglang.srt.megakernels` and `sglang.srt.monokernels` are removed.
  - The plugins import the new locations first and fall back to the old ones for earlier SGLang: sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega#21 and sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#25, both merged.
  - The pins move to those merge commits:
    - `SGL_NVIDIA_MEGA_COMMIT` becomes `6fd7ac3` in both CUDA Dockerfiles. Main pins `3333e4c` (#46030), an ancestor of `6fd7ac3`.
    - The `sgl-amd-mono` pin in `pyproject_other.toml` becomes `05e0bb0`.
- **`KernelBackend.PLUGIN`.** Adds the enum value and a `forward_plugin` hook on `BaseFusedOp`, placed after KDA/CAKE in `DEFAULT_PRIORITY`. The namespace test pairs `plugin_kernels/` with this backend.
- **`--monokernel-backend amd` → `--enable-amd-monokernel`.** The flag becomes a boolean next to `--enable-nvidia-megakernel`.
  - `--monokernel-backend amd` stays as a deprecated spelling: it warns and sets the new flag. Any other value is rejected.
  - The field keeps its slot in `POSITIONAL_FIELD_ORDER`.
  - Both spellings also work in `--config` YAML files. Previously the merger accepted only `store`/`store_true` actions, which rejected the deprecated alias and, through the shared dest, the new key too.
    - The merger now passes single-value actions as `--flag value`.
    - A key stays usable when a supported flag also reads it.
    - A regression test covers `monokernel-backend: amd`, `enable-amd-monokernel: true` / `false`, and both CLI spellings. Before the fix, the three YAML cases raise `ValueError`.
  - The resolution hook is renamed `handle_amd_monokernel`.
  - Error messages, the server-args doc, the DeepSeek-V4.1 cookbook and the ROCm Dockerfile comment are updated.
- **Docs.** `kernels/README.md`, `plugin_kernels/README.md` and the kernel-organization skill describe the split.

No runtime behavior changes: the default path is untouched, and the megakernel and monokernel code is the same code at new paths.

**Not covered: the MSA plugin.** The MiniMax-M3.1 cookbook (#45924) serves the MSA plugin with `--monokernel-backend msa`. On this PR that value is rejected, and the plugin's `sglang.srt.monokernels` imports fail. That plugin is moving off the monokernel name separately.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs: 4x GB300 (sm_103), `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`, plugins at the pinned commits (sgl-nvidia-mega `6fd7ac3`, sgl-amd-mono `05e0bb0`).

The PR content was tested at `7311b92f02`, which has main `6e667c4310` merged. The head has main `3ea7e210d2` merged instead; that merge changed nothing in this PR except resolving the NVIDIA pin conflict.

### Tests and plugin loading

- **43 CPU-relevant test files**, each run in its own process: `unit/kernels/**`, `unit/server_args/**`, `unit/model_loader/**`, the moved tests, `test_dspark_draft_block`, `test_runtime_context` and others.
  - Main `6e667c4310` and this PR fail the same single case.
  - The 5 moved test files pass.
- **Plugins through their real entry points.**
  - On this PR, `sglang.srt.megakernels` is gone, and both plugins register from the new locations.
  - On main, they register from the old ones.
  - Either way, the NVIDIA DeepSeek-V4.1 target and draft specs resolve to `MegakernelSpec`, and all six AMD specs resolve on `gfx950`.
- **The plugins' own `test/unit`.**
  - sgl-amd-mono `05e0bb0`: 5 failed, 124 passed on both main and this PR, the same five. They are GLM-5.3 spec cases.
  - sgl-nvidia-mega `6fd7ac3`: the Kimi K3 tests fail on both.
    - On main they fail because the hybrid views from #45406 are missing. With `--continue-on-collection-errors`, that is 22 failed, 162 passed, 1 error, all Kimi K3.
    - On this PR they also fail because `kimi_k3` imports `sglang.srt.megakernels` with no fallback. #45406 has to move those views to `srt/kernel_plugins/nvidia/binding.py` anyway, and `kimi_k3` should then import them new-path-first, as DeepSeek-V4.1 does.

### The real megakernel, end to end

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, served with the plugin README's command (TP4, DSpark block 5, `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` and the three required env vars):

| | main `b453996b7d` | this PR on `b453996b7d` (`48b0063ff6`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NVIDIA megakernel: active` (target and DSpark draft specs, 4 ranks) | 8 lines | 8 lines |
| `draft proposal engaged` during graph capture | 108 | 108 |
| GSM8K, sgl-eval 0.1.3, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, no thinking, seed 0 | 0.985 | 0.990 |

On main `6e667c4310`, the same command fails with or without this PR, identically:
- Both activate (8 lines).
- Both then fail during the first verify-graph capture, also with `--max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8`. SGLang's DeepSeek-V4 indexer, reached through `view.low_ratio_sources`, hits `assert A.shape[:-1] == As.shape[:-1]` in the fp8 `wq_b` GEMM.

A partial bisect puts that regression between `bb9e9d5632` (good) and `b588aa39e9` (bad, #45921). The head after the latest main merge was not run on GPU.

Not run: monokernel serving on gfx950. The AMD side was checked statically and on CPU only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A: no kernel or forward change.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (namespace pairing test extended; moved tests kept; config-flag regression test)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (N/A: no numerics change)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+# `plugin_kernels` — plugin kernel backend
+
+The contracts of external kernel libraries that load as SGLang plugins and
+replace a model's step with kernels specialized for one model, configuration
+and platform. Today they serve small-batch decode and verify steps; prefill or
+high-throughput specializations fit here too. `KernelBackend.PLUGIN` records
+them; the [kernels README](../README.md) explains how a backend relates to the
+operator groups. These are kernel plugins, not the platform plugins that add a
+device.
+
+## Layout
+
+The code is split at the kernel/runtime boundary.
+
+```
+kernels/plugin_kernels/      # what a plugin implements; imports nothing from srt
+  <hardware>/spec.py         #   registration, API version, requirements,
+                             #   capabilities and widths, build/forward contract
+  <hardware>/<model>/        #   thin wrappers around the library's kernels
+srt/kernel_plugins/          # SGLang's integration
+  <hardware>/binding.py      #   startup checks, weight observation, TP agreement,
+                             #   CUDA graph coverage, forward dispatch and fallback,
+                             #   and the runtime state handed to the plugin
+```
+
+| Hardware | Server flag | Library |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `nvidia/` | `--enable-nvidia-megakernel` | [sgl-nvidia-mega](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-nvidia-mega) |
+| `amd/` | `--enable-amd-monokernel` | [sgl-amd-mono](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono) |
+
+## How a plugin runs
+
+A library registers its specs through the `sglang.srt.plugins` entry point.
+With its server flag set, `srt/kernel_plugins/<hardware>/binding.py`:
+- checks the spec against the resolved configuration at argument resolution,
+  before the weights load, and stops the server listing every reason it cannot
+  serve;
+- builds the spec once the model is prepared;
+- replaces that model's forward for the steps the spec covers; every other step
+  runs the model's own forward.
+
+The kernels stay in their libraries, which import the contract from
+`sglang.kernels.plugin_kernels.<hardware>` and, in their tests, the integration
+from `sglang.srt.kernel_plugins.<hardware>`. Unit tests are in
+`test/registered/unit/kernel_plugins/<hardware>/`.
+
+## Operators
+
+An external kernel exposed as an operator registers into its logical group
+(`ops/<group>/__init__.py`) with `KernelSpec(op="<group>.<name>",
+backend=KernelBackend.PLUGIN,
+target="sglang.kernels.plugin_kernels.<hardware>.<model>.<module>:<function>")`;
+callers import the `ops.<group>` facade.

reviews.body:
AMD side looks good to me. I checked the head (`63a30a1f`) against current main and against sgl-amd-mono at the pinned `b27d604` and at its main:

- It merges cleanly into current main. Outside the aliases, nothing still imports `sglang.srt.monokernels`, and nothing outside the deprecated flag reads `monokernel_backend`.

Notes:
sgl-amd-mono's contract test needs the same read-through as sgl-nvidia-mega#21. I'll open that PR.

[Codex]: The plugin naming and backend classification make sense to me, but I would suggest separating the plugin contract from the serving-runtime integration before moving the whole interface into `kernels/`.

A useful boundary would be:

- `kernels/plugin_kernels/`: spec registration, API versions, capability/shape declarations, build/forward contracts, and any thin kernel wrappers. The actual implementations can remain in `sgl-nvidia-mega` and `sgl-amd-mono`.
- `srt/`: interpreting server configuration, observing checkpoint loading and retaining weight copies, coordinating TP ranks, deriving CUDA graph capture coverage, installing model-forward dispatch/fallback, and enforcing weight-update restrictions.

In particular, most of the moved `runtime.py` code manages the model's execution and resource lifecycle. Keeping that in `srt/` would avoid making whole-step plugins an exception to the kernel/runtime dependency boundary. This does not require breaking up a megakernel or changing its whole-step execution: the runtime adapter can still build the plugin once and route each supported step to it.

`guards.py` and `binding.py` also cross this boundary: capability checks and the interface presented to a plugin can belong with the contract, while reading/resolving ServerArgs and assembling bindings from the model runner, KV cache, and process groups belong in the runtime adapter. Merely moving `spec.py` would not remove existing model/config coupling; narrowing those inputs can be incremental rather than requiring a new generic abstraction in this PR.

For this refactor, could we unify the contracts and backend naming under `kernels/`, while retaining the model integration and lifecycle hooks under `srt/`? That would let future changes to model loading or CUDA graph planning stay in the serving layer without making the kernel interface responsible for those internals. Also, the current whole-step integrations still install model-forward hooks rather than dispatching through `BaseFusedOp.forward_plugin`, so this separation would make the two integration paths clearer.

[Codex]: The updated split addresses my architectural concern: plugin contracts and registration live under `kernels/plugin_kernels/`, while configuration handling, model dispatch, and resource lifecycle management remain under `srt/kernel_plugins/`. This boundary looks good to me.

One remaining correctness issue is detailed inline: the deprecated AMD argument currently causes both the old and new YAML configuration keys to be rejected.

Also, the removal of the old import paths makes the documented plugin-update order a merge prerequisite. At this head, the NVIDIA pin is still `d47deb3` and the AMD pin is `b27d604`. Please ensure the compatible plugin changes are merged and both pins are updated in the resulting SGLang tree before this lands; validation against plugin PR checkouts alone does not establish compatibility with the pinned installations.
In general the design is good to me. Please make sure the compatibility is ok.
